_doc: HMTc Category 23 (Food-Contact Consumer Goods and Kitchenware) compiler config. Method v2.0, government-limit-only. THE NATIVE BASIS OF THIS ENTIRE CATEGORY IS SPECIFIC ELEMENT MIGRATION INTO FOOD OR A FOOD SIMULANT, in µg/kg of food, per the Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II convention. The register contains exactly ONE instrument family expressed in that basis: the EU 10/2011 Annex II element list (Pb, Cd, tAs and tHg not detectable at their stated detection limits; total Cr not detectable with a 3.6 mg/kg relaxation on documented Cr(VI) exclusion, which HMTc declines; Ni SML 0.02 mg/kg food; Al SML 1 mg/kg food; no tin entry). Every published number on every row in this category traces to that family, either directly where the food-contact surface is a plastic within the instrument's scope, or by a disclosed read-across where the food-contact surface is a polymeric material the instrument expressly excludes (silicone, Art. 2(2)(c); ion-exchange resin, Art. 2(2)(a)) or does not reach (cured liquid-applied coatings and lacquers, a Regulation 1935/2004 Annex I family with no specific measure; paper and board; wood). WHERE THE FOOD-CONTACT SURFACE IS METAL, ALLOY, CERAMIC GLAZE, VITREOUS ENAMEL OR GLASS, THE ROW IS A CONTROL AND NO NUMBER IS INVENTED. That is not a shortcut: the release regimes that actually govern those families are absent from the register (EU Council Directive 84/500/EEC on ceramic articles as amended by 2005/31/EC; the US FDA compliance-policy guides on lead in ceramicware and decorated glassware; California Proposition 65 tableware consent judgments; the Council of Europe metals-and-alloys technical guide; SDWA s.1417 lead-free and NSF/ANSI 61 for water-contact materials; China GB 4806 series), and they are recorded as register gaps rather than replaced with a plastics value. THREE FOREIGN BASES appear in this category only as disclosed companions and are never published as a ceiling: the FOOD basis (canned-food tin maximum levels, which limit the contents of the can and not the can), the MATERIAL-CONTENT basis (Japan Notice 370 and Korea MFDS 2024-29 percent-by-weight lead in food-contact metals, solder and tin plating; CPSIA total lead in substrate; EU REACH Annex XVII cadmium restrictions; RoHS homogeneous-material limits), and the WATER basis (drinking-water parametric values, which limit the water as delivered and not the device). A fourth basis is excluded outright: the TOY article-extraction basis (EU 2009/48 Annex II Part III Categories I to III and ASTM F963 soluble limits) measures element migration from scraped-off or coated toy material into 0.07 M hydrochloric acid expressed per kg of MATERIAL, is orders of magnitude looser than a per-kg-of-food migration limit, and is barred from this category by every row's basis_guard. ONE DELIBERATE DEPARTURE from the default convention is recorded here for audit: total chromium is published as a FIRM cell rather than a screen on the 10/2011-anchored rows, because Annex II point 2 sets total chromium at not detectable precisely so that hexavalent chromium need not be assumed absent, and relaxes to 3.6 mg/kg food only on documented Cr(VI) exclusion; the non-detect branch is therefore the Cr(VI)-conservative form of the requirement rather than a Cr(III)-dominated artefact, HMTc declines the relaxation, and the Cr-VI cell is speciation-bounded by it. On the control rows, by contrast, total chromium is a control and its rationale states plainly that it is a screening determination and not a protective ceiling, and Cr-VI is a control rather than a not-material determination because no published parent bounds it there. Species never replace totals anywhere in this category: iAs cannot satisfy tAs, MeHg cannot satisfy tHg, Cr-VI cannot satisfy total Cr.

_category.name: Food-Contact Consumer Goods and Kitchenware
_category.anchor: EU food-contact framework Regulation 1935/2004 with Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II specific migration limits as the only element-migration instrument in the register; polymer-surface rows anchor it directly or by disclosed read-across, and metal, alloy, ceramic-glaze, vitreous-enamel and glass rows are controls because their dedicated release regimes are not yet ingested.
_category.basis_family: Specific element migration INTO FOOD OR A FOOD SIMULANT, µg/kg of food (Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II convention). Bases are never conflated in this category. A migration ceiling is never published as a content ceiling and a content, food or water ceiling is never published as a migration ceiling. The three foreign bases that surround these rows appear only as disclosed companions: FOOD basis (canned-food tin maximum levels, on the contents not the article), MATERIAL-CONTENT basis (Japan Notice 370 and Korea MFDS 2024-29 percent-by-weight lead in food-contact metals, solder and tin plating; CPSIA total lead in substrate; EU REACH Annex XVII cadmium; RoHS homogeneous materials), and WATER basis (drinking-water parametric values, on the water as delivered not the device). The TOY article-extraction basis (EU 2009/48 Annex II Part III Categories I to III, ASTM F963 soluble limits, per kg of MATERIAL into 0.07 M HCl) is barred from every row by basis_guard.
_category.method_label: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only): the strictest applicable sovereign maximum for this exact product form expressed as specific element migration into food or a food simulant; a disclosed read-across from the nearest applicable sovereign value in the same basis where the food-contact material family is expressly excluded from or not reached by that instrument; a substantiated not-material determination; or a control. No cell is occurrence-derived, and no cell borrows a value across a basis.
_category.method_note: TWO CATEGORY RULES govern every row. (1) THE MATERIAL-FAMILY RULE: a row's published ceiling is anchored only where a sovereign instrument governs element migration into food from that row's PRINCIPAL food-contact material family. Polymer surfaces anchor EU 10/2011 Annex II directly, or by disclosed read-across where the instrument expressly excludes the polymer (silicone under Art. 2(2)(c), ion-exchange resin under Art. 2(2)(a)) or does not reach it (cured liquid-applied coatings, paper and board, wood). Metal, alloy, ceramic-glaze, vitreous-enamel and glass surfaces have no sovereign migration ceiling in the register, so those rows are controls with mandatory testing and no invented number. (2) THE COMPONENT RULE: every food-contact COMPONENT of an article is held to the regime of its own material family, and where a component's family has no sovereign ceiling that component is under control. A row's published cells state the ceiling for its principal food-contact material; the component plan names the other components, the regime each falls under, and which component is expected to bind. A result from a non-binding component does not represent the article: a can body wall does not represent its seam, a vacuum bottle wall does not represent its base-plug solder, a plain tumbler does not represent a decorated one, a blender jar does not represent its blade assembly, and a cold reservoir does not represent a post-descaling draw.

food-packaging-cans-lids.name: Cans/lids
food-packaging-cans-lids.native_basis: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food), Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II convention
food-packaging-cans-lids.native_basis_label: specific element migration INTO FOOD OR A FOOD SIMULANT from the polymeric food-contact surface, µg/kg of food, determined by the Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex III to V simulant, temperature and contact-time conventions. This is a MIGRATION basis and not a total-content basis: no cell on this row limits how much of an element the material CONTAINS, and no cell on this row is expressed per kg of material.
food-packaging-cans-lids.scope_note: The finished sealed can and its end as filled and processed, including hot-fill and retort sterilised product. The food-contact surface of a modern food can is the cured organic interior lacquer, so the published ceilings read across from the plastics migration instrument. Where a can interior is UNCOATED tinplate, or where the lacquer is breached, that configuration falls to the metal-article release control regime instead, and the tin cell is a control on every configuration. Tin is the defining pathway for this row and the canned-food tin maximum levels are a FOOD-basis companion on the contents, disclosed here and never published as this row's migration ceiling.
food-packaging-cans-lids.material: Three-piece or two-piece tinplate or electrolytically chromium-coated steel, or aluminium, with a cured organic interior lacquer (epoxy-phenolic, polyester, acrylic or oleoresinous); welded or, historically, soldered side seam; compound-lined ends.
food-packaging-cans-lids.components: Sample and report separately: (1) interior lacquer on the body wall; (2) interior lacquer on the end panel and the double-seam area, where coating coverage is thinnest; (3) exposed tinplate or chromium-coated steel at the side seam and at score or easy-open features; (4) end-compound sealing gasket; (5) any solder at the side seam on legacy or imported stock; (6) interior printing or coding inks. Report the seam and end-panel result as the binding component; a body-wall-only result does not represent the article.
food-packaging-cans-lids.audit_scope: food.contact|food contact|plastic food|utensil|cookware|cooking utensil|kitchen|tableware|crockery|ceramic|porcelain|earthenware|glaze|enamel|glassware|hollowware|packaging and containers|food-contact surface
food-packaging-cans-lids.basis_guard_note: Only an instrument expressed as specific element migration into food or a food simulant may anchor a cell on this row. The guard exists to reject the three foreign bases that surround this category and would otherwise look plausible: the FOOD basis (canned-food tin maximum levels, which limit the contents and not the article), the MATERIAL-CONTENT basis (CPSIA total lead in substrate, EU REACH Annex XVII cadmium percent-by-weight restrictions, RoHS homogeneous-material limits, Japan Notice 370 and Korea MFDS percent-by-weight lead in food-contact metals), and the ARTICLE-EXTRACTION basis of the toy regime (EU 2009/48 Annex II Part III and ASTM F963 soluble limits, which are element migration from scraped-off or coated TOY material into 0.07 M hydrochloric acid, expressed per kg of MATERIAL, not per kg of food). Any of those would fail this guard and resolve to a gap rather than publish in the wrong basis. On this control row the guard is declaratory as well as operative: it records the only basis in which a future ingested instrument would be allowed to supply this row's numbers, so that a content limit, a food limit, a water limit or a plastics specific migration limit cannot later be dropped in as this row's release ceiling. The plastics clause is deliberately absent from this guard: a Reg (EU) 10/2011 value named here would fail the guard and resolve to a gap.

read_across.label: read-across of the EU 10/2011 Annex II point 2 lead non-detect requirement (0.01 mg/kg food)
read_across.substantiation: The exact cell is unregulated: the food-contact surface of a food can is a cured organic coating, and coatings and varnishes are a Regulation 1935/2004 Annex I material family for which the EU has adopted no specific measure, while Regulation (EU) 10/2011 reaches plastic layers and plastic coatings in multi-material multi-layer articles but is not written for a liquid-applied cured lacquer. The nearest applicable sovereign value in the identical basis is therefore the EU 10/2011 Annex II element requirement for a polymeric food-contact layer, and it is read across with disclosure. The read-across holds the basis constant: source and destination are the same measured quantity, specific element migration into food or a food simulant in µg/kg food, determined by the same test conventions. The analogy is on basis and exposure endpoint, not on material identity, and it is disclosed as a read-across rather than presented as a limit written for this article. Lead is on the Annex II point 2 not-detectable list, so the published ceiling is the 0.01 mg/kg food detection limit and not a positive migration allowance. Applied to the can, this ceiling governs the lacquered interior surface as the food-contact surface; the uncoated-tinplate and breached-coating configurations are handled by the component plan under the metal-article release control regime, and the tin pathway is a control on every configuration. This is a migration ceiling on the food or simulant and is never reported as a limit on the material's lead content; the material-content instruments (US CPSIA total lead in children's-product substrate, Japan Notice 370 and Korea MFDS 2024-29 percent-by-weight lead in food-contact metals and solder) are separate obligations in a different basis and are not this cell.

read_across.substantiation: The exact cell is unregulated: the food-contact surface of a food can is a cured organic coating, and coatings and varnishes are a Regulation 1935/2004 Annex I material family for which the EU has adopted no specific measure, while Regulation (EU) 10/2011 reaches plastic layers and plastic coatings in multi-material multi-layer articles but is not written for a liquid-applied cured lacquer. tAs.basis_label: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)

not_material.rationale: Inorganic arsenic is a dietary speciation with no separate food-contact-material instrument anywhere in the credible set: every food-contact element requirement is written on total arsenic. Arsenic migrating from a polymeric food-contact article is in any case inorganic, so the total-arsenic non-detect requirement is simultaneously the tightest achievable inorganic-arsenic ceiling and bounds this cell by identity. No separate inorganic-arsenic ceiling is published, and inorganic arsenic never substitutes for the total-arsenic cell.
not_material.bounded_by: tAs (read-across of eu_10_2011_tas_sml_nd, total arsenic not detectable at 0.01 mg/kg food)
not_material.reference_method: Total-arsenic migration determination per the tAs cell; reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation by HPLC-ICP-MS on the migration extract only where total arsenic is detected at or above the detection limit.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2 sets the element requirement as a specific migration requirement on the food or food simulant, not as a limit on the material's element content. No credible sovereign sets a species-specific migration limit for this cell.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU (Reg (EU) 1935/2004 framework + Annex I material families; Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II element list, as amended by 2016/1416 and 2020/1245); UK (retained Reg 10/2011); US (FDA food-contact substances, 21 CFR 174-190: no element migration ceiling for these elements); Codex (no food-contact-material standard); AU-NZ (FSANZ Food Standards Code 1.4.3 and 3.2.2: no element migration ceiling); Canada (Food and Drugs Act s.4 / letter-of-no-objection route, no numeric element migration ceiling); Hong Kong (Cap 132 subsidiary legislation: food limits only).

read_across.label: read-across of the EU 10/2011 Annex II point 2 total-mercury non-detect requirement (0.01 mg/kg food)
read_across.substantiation: The exact cell is unregulated: the food-contact surface of a food can is a cured organic coating, and coatings and varnishes are a Regulation 1935/2004 Annex I material family for which the EU has adopted no specific measure, while Regulation (EU) 10/2011 reaches plastic layers and plastic coatings in multi-material multi-layer articles but is not written for a liquid-applied cured lacquer. The nearest applicable sovereign value in the identical basis is therefore the EU 10/2011 Annex II element requirement for a polymeric food-contact layer, and it is read across with disclosure. The read-across holds the basis constant: source and destination are the same measured quantity, specific element migration into food or a food simulant in µg/kg food, determined by the same test conventions. The analogy is on basis and exposure endpoint, not on material identity, and it is disclosed as a read-across rather than presented as a limit written for this article. Mercury is on the Annex II point 2 not-detectable list, stated as the total element. Applied to the can, this ceiling governs the lacquered interior surface as the food-contact surface; the uncoated-tinplate and breached-coating configurations are handled by the component plan under the metal-article release control regime, and the tin pathway is a control on every configuration.

tHg.basis_label: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is formed by microbial methylation in aquatic food chains. A cured polymer, a fired glaze, a metal alloy and a coated article contain no methylation pathway, and no credible sovereign sets a methylmercury requirement for any food-contact material. The total-mercury non-detect requirement bounds any organomercury fraction that could be present. No separate methylmercury ceiling is published, and methylmercury never substitutes for the total-mercury cell.
not_material.bounded_by: tHg (read-across of eu_10_2011_thg_sml_nd, total mercury not detectable at 0.01 mg/kg food)
not_material.reference_method: Total-mercury migration determination per the tHg cell; reflex methylmercury speciation by GC-ICP-MS on the migration extract only where total mercury is detected at or above the detection limit.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2 sets the element requirement as a specific migration requirement on the food or food simulant, not as a limit on the material's element content. No credible sovereign sets a species-specific migration limit for this cell.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU (Reg (EU) 1935/2004 framework + Annex I material families; Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II element list, as amended by 2016/1416 and 2020/1245); UK (retained Reg 10/2011); US (FDA food-contact substances, 21 CFR 174-190: no element migration ceiling for these elements); Codex (no food-contact-material standard); AU-NZ (FSANZ Food Standards Code 1.4.3 and 3.2.2: no element migration ceiling); Canada (Food and Drugs Act s.4 / letter-of-no-objection route, no numeric element migration ceiling); Hong Kong (Cap 132 subsidiary legislation: food limits only).

read_across.label: read-across of the EU 10/2011 Annex II point 1 nickel SML (0.02 mg/kg food)
read_across.substantiation: The exact cell is unregulated: the food-contact surface of a food can is a cured organic coating, and coatings and varnishes are a Regulation 1935/2004 Annex I material family for which the EU has adopted no specific measure, while Regulation (EU) 10/2011 reaches plastic layers and plastic coatings in multi-material multi-layer articles but is not written for a liquid-applied cured lacquer. The nearest applicable sovereign value in the identical basis is therefore the EU 10/2011 Annex II element requirement for a polymeric food-contact layer, and it is read across with disclosure. The read-across holds the basis constant: source and destination are the same measured quantity, specific element migration into food or a food simulant in µg/kg food, determined by the same test conventions. The analogy is on basis and exposure endpoint, not on material identity, and it is disclosed as a read-across rather than presented as a limit written for this article. Nickel carries a positive specific migration limit of 0.02 mg/kg food, the tightest positive SML in the Annex II element list. Applied to the can, this ceiling governs the lacquered interior surface as the food-contact surface; the uncoated-tinplate and breached-coating configurations are handled by the component plan under the metal-article release control regime, and the tin pathway is a control on every configuration. This value governs the polymeric food-contact surface only; where a food-contact component of the article is a nickel-bearing alloy, that component sits in the alloy-release control regime described in this row's component plan, because the plastics SML was not written for and is not achievable by a bare stainless-steel surface.

Ni.basis_label: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)

control.rationale: Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II lists no tin entry, and no credible sovereign sets a tin migration or release ceiling for a can, a can end or any other food-contact article. Tin is the defining pathway of this row, so a control here is a mandatory determination and not a shrug: tin dissolves from exposed tinplate wherever the interior lacquer is absent, thin or breached, which is why the sovereign response to canned-food tin is a maximum level on the FOOD rather than on the article. Those food maximum levels (EU Reg 2023/915 at 200 mg/kg for canned foods and 100 mg/kg for canned beverages, Codex CXS 193 and FSANZ Schedule 19 at 250 mg/kg, and 50 mg/kg for canned infant and young-child products) are disclosed as a companion obligation on the contents. They are a FOOD basis, they are measured in the food and not in a simulant against the article, and republishing one of them as this row's migration ceiling would be the exact basis conflation this category's guard exists to prevent.
control.reference_method: EN 1186 / EN 13130 food-simulant migration testing on the finished article under its worst foreseeable use conditions (simulant, temperature and contact time selected per Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex III and Annex V; for repeat-use articles the third successive migration result governs), with ICP-MS determination of the element in the simulant. Tin determined additionally on the finished packed product at the end of the declared shelf life, and on the seam and end-panel extraction separately, because tin dissolution is progressive and localised.

read_across.label: read-across of the EU 10/2011 Annex II point 1 aluminium SML (1 mg/kg food)
read_across.substantiation: The exact cell is unregulated: the food-contact surface of a food can is a cured organic coating, and coatings and varnishes are a Regulation 1935/2004 Annex I material family for which the EU has adopted no specific measure, while Regulation (EU) 10/2011 reaches plastic layers and plastic coatings in multi-material multi-layer articles but is not written for a liquid-applied cured lacquer. The nearest applicable sovereign value in the identical basis is therefore the EU 10/2011 Annex II element requirement for a polymeric food-contact layer, and it is read across with disclosure. The read-across holds the basis constant: source and destination are the same measured quantity, specific element migration into food or a food simulant in µg/kg food, determined by the same test conventions. The analogy is on basis and exposure endpoint, not on material identity, and it is disclosed as a read-across rather than presented as a limit written for this article. Aluminium carries a positive specific migration limit of 1 mg/kg food, added by Reg (EU) 2016/1416. Applied to the can, this ceiling governs the lacquered interior surface as the food-contact surface; the uncoated-tinplate and breached-coating configurations are handled by the component plan under the metal-article release control regime, and the tin pathway is a control on every configuration. This value governs the polymeric food-contact surface; it is not applied to an aluminium metal article, because an instrument written for plastics did not contemplate an article whose food-contact surface is the element itself.

read_across.label: read-across of the EU 10/2011 Annex II point 2 total-chromium non-detect requirement (0.01 mg/kg food), relaxation declined
read_across.substantiation: The exact cell is unregulated: the food-contact surface of a food can is a cured organic coating, and coatings and varnishes are a Regulation 1935/2004 Annex I material family for which the EU has adopted no specific measure, while Regulation (EU) 10/2011 reaches plastic layers and plastic coatings in multi-material multi-layer articles but is not written for a liquid-applied cured lacquer. The nearest applicable sovereign value in the identical basis is therefore the EU 10/2011 Annex II element requirement for a polymeric food-contact layer, and it is read across with disclosure. The read-across holds the basis constant: source and destination are the same measured quantity, specific element migration into food or a food simulant in µg/kg food, determined by the same test conventions. The analogy is on basis and exposure endpoint, not on material identity, and it is disclosed as a read-across rather than presented as a limit written for this article. This total-chromium cell is deliberately published as a firm ceiling rather than the usual non-protective total-chromium screen, and the reason is structural to the instrument. Annex II point 2 as amended by Reg (EU) 2020/1245 sets total chromium at not detectable and permits a relaxed 3.6 mg/kg food limit only where the operator documents that chromium(VI) is absent. The non-detect branch therefore exists precisely because hexavalent chromium cannot be assumed absent, which makes it the hexavalent-chromium-conservative form of the requirement rather than a chromium(III)-dominated artefact. HMTc publishes the non-detect branch and declines the relaxation, and the hexavalent-chromium cell is bounded by this value. Applied to the can, this ceiling governs the lacquered interior surface as the food-contact surface; the uncoated-tinplate and breached-coating configurations are handled by the component plan under the metal-article release control regime, and the tin pathway is a control on every configuration.

Cr.basis_label: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)

not_material.rationale: Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2 controls hexavalent chromium through the total-chromium requirement rather than through a separate species limit: total chromium must be not detectable, and the relaxed 3.6 mg/kg food value becomes available only where the operator documents that chromium(VI) is absent. HMTc declines that relaxation, so every certified article is held to total chromium not detectable at 0.01 mg/kg food, which bounds hexavalent chromium at or below the same value. No credible sovereign sets a hexavalent-chromium migration limit for a food-contact material, so no separate species ceiling is published; hexavalent chromium never substitutes for the total-chromium cell.
not_material.bounded_by: Cr (read-across of eu_10_2011_crtotal_sml_nd, total chromium not detectable at 0.01 mg/kg food, relaxation declined)
not_material.reference_method: Total-chromium migration determination per the Cr cell; reflex hexavalent-chromium speciation by ion-chromatography ICP-MS on the migration extract where total chromium is detected at or above the detection limit, and on any chromate-conversion-coated or passivated food-contact component regardless of the total result.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2 sets the element requirement as a specific migration requirement on the food or food simulant, not as a limit on the material's element content. No credible sovereign sets a species-specific migration limit for this cell.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU (Reg (EU) 1935/2004 framework + Annex I material families; Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II element list, as amended by 2016/1416 and 2020/1245); UK (retained Reg 10/2011); US (FDA food-contact substances, 21 CFR 174-190: no element migration ceiling for these elements); Codex (no food-contact-material standard); AU-NZ (FSANZ Food Standards Code 1.4.3 and 3.2.2: no element migration ceiling); Canada (Food and Drugs Act s.4 / letter-of-no-objection route, no numeric element migration ceiling); Hong Kong (Cap 132 subsidiary legislation: food limits only).

food-packaging-cans-lids.cross_reference: Category 9 (Infant and Child Contact Products) governs any article in this row that is marketed for ages 0-5; the taxonomy boundary rule routes infant bottles, nipples and toddler drinkware there even though they are food-contact items.

food-packaging-glass-jars.name: Glass jars
food-packaging-glass-jars.native_basis: element release from the glaze, enamel or glass into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
food-packaging-glass-jars.native_basis_label: element RELEASE FROM THE GLAZE, VITREOUS ENAMEL OR GLASS NETWORK INTO FOOD OR A FOOD SIMULANT, µg/kg of food, determined by the 4 percent (v/v) acetic acid filled-article or contact-surface extraction convention used for this material family, with decoration within 20 mm of the lip determined separately. This is the glaze-and-glass RELEASE basis; it is deliberately NOT the Reg (EU) 10/2011 plastics-simulant convention, and a plastics specific migration limit is never substituted for a release limit on this family.
food-packaging-glass-jars.scope_note: The glass container as filled, together with its closure system. The principal food-contact material is the glass network, whose element release regime is absent from the register, so the row is a control. The closure's plasticised sealing compound is a plastic gasket in a cap or closure and is directly within Reg (EU) 10/2011 Art. 2(1)(d), so that component is bound by the plastics migration ceilings as a companion obligation reported under the caps-and-closures row; the metal closure shell falls to the metal-article release control regime.
food-packaging-glass-jars.material: Soda-lime-silica container glass body; metal (tinplate or aluminium) twist or lug closure with a plasticised sealing compound; occasional applied ceramic labelling or exterior decoration.
food-packaging-glass-jars.components: Sample and report separately: (1) interior glass surface, filled-article extraction; (2) plasticised sealing compound of the closure, migration test against the actual food or the appropriate simulant; (3) interior surface of the metal closure shell, including any lacquer and any exposed cut edge; (4) applied ceramic labelling or exterior decoration where it lies within 20 mm of the sealing surface or the lip.
food-packaging-glass-jars.audit_scope: food.contact|food contact|plastic food|utensil|cookware|cooking utensil|kitchen|tableware|crockery|ceramic|porcelain|earthenware|glaze|enamel|glassware|hollowware|packaging and containers|food-contact surface
food-packaging-glass-jars.basis_guard: element release from the glaze, enamel or glass into food
food-packaging-glass-jars.basis_guard_note: Only an instrument expressed as specific element migration into food or a food simulant may anchor a cell on this row. The guard exists to reject the three foreign bases that surround this category and would otherwise look plausible: the FOOD basis (canned-food tin maximum levels, which limit the contents and not the article), the MATERIAL-CONTENT basis (CPSIA total lead in substrate, EU REACH Annex XVII cadmium percent-by-weight restrictions, RoHS homogeneous-material limits, Japan Notice 370 and Korea MFDS percent-by-weight lead in food-contact metals), and the ARTICLE-EXTRACTION basis of the toy regime (EU 2009/48 Annex II Part III and ASTM F963 soluble limits, which are element migration from scraped-off or coated TOY material into 0.07 M hydrochloric acid, expressed per kg of MATERIAL, not per kg of food). Any of those would fail this guard and resolve to a gap rather than publish in the wrong basis. On this control row the guard is declaratory as well as operative: it records the only basis in which a future ingested instrument would be allowed to supply this row's numbers, so that a content limit, a food limit, a water limit or a plastics specific migration limit cannot later be dropped in as this row's release ceiling. The plastics clause is deliberately absent from this guard: a Reg (EU) 10/2011 value named here would fail the guard and resolve to a gap.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign release ceiling for this material family is present in the HMTc regulatory register. Glazed ceramic, vitreous enamel, glass and applied decoration are governed in the real world by a dedicated lead-and-cadmium release regime (EU Council Directive 84/500/EEC as amended by 2005/31/EC for ceramic articles, and the US FDA compliance-policy guides on lead in ceramicware and decorated glassware), and by California Proposition 65 consent judgments on tableware. None of those instruments has been ingested into data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, and this build refuses to substitute the plastics specific migration limits for a glaze-release limit: the two are different extractions on different material families and the substitution would be a basis conflation. The cell is a control until the release regime is ingested through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway, and the gap is recorded. Lead is the dominant pathway for this material family: lead-fluxed and lead-bisilicate glazes, lead-bearing on-glaze enamels and applied decoration, and under-fired or acid-attacked glaze surfaces all release lead into acidic food. It is the single cell where the absent release regime matters most, and the gap is recorded rather than papered over with a plastics value. On a glass jar the tin route is the TINPLATE CLOSURE SHELL rather than the glass, and the canned-food tin maximum levels are a FOOD-basis companion on the packed contents that is never published as this row's release ceiling. For a glass jar the release surface is the glass network itself and the applied-decoration surface where present; the closure gasket and the closure shell are separate components with their own regimes, recorded in the component plan and never averaged into this row's result.
control.reference_method: Release testing on the filled or contact-surface article using 4 percent (v/v) acetic acid at the article's stated use temperature and duration (the release convention used for glazed, enamelled and glass food-contact articles), ICP-MS determination in the extract, with a separate determination on any decoration lying within 20 mm of the lip or on any interior decoration.

food-packaging-plastic-tubs.name: Plastic tubs
food-packaging-plastic-tubs.native_basis: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food), Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II convention
food-packaging-plastic-tubs.native_basis_label: specific element migration INTO FOOD OR A FOOD SIMULANT from the polymeric food-contact surface, µg/kg of food, determined by the Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex III to V simulant, temperature and contact-time conventions. This is a MIGRATION basis and not a total-content basis: no cell on this row limits how much of an element the material CONTAINS, and no cell on this row is expressed per kg of material.
food-packaging-plastic-tubs.scope_note: Rigid plastic containers for retail food filling. Materials consisting exclusively of plastics, directly within the scope of Reg (EU) 10/2011 Art. 2(1)(a). Recycled-content tubs (recovered PET or PVC) are within scope of this row and are the configuration where element migration is most likely, so the component plan requires them to be tested as their own lot rather than represented by a virgin-resin result.
food-packaging-plastic-tubs.material: Injection-moulded or thermoformed polypropylene, polystyrene, PET or HDPE, with in-mould-labelled or printed decoration and a peel or snap lid.
food-packaging-plastic-tubs.components: Sample and report separately: (1) tub body interior surface; (2) in-mould label or printed decoration where it is on the food-contact side; (3) peel-seal or snap lid food-contact layer; (4) any recycled-content resin stream, tested as its own lot; (5) masterbatch colourant, verified for lead chromate, cadmium sulfoselenide and chrome-green pigment content.

Pb.label: Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2: lead not detectable in the food or simulant, detection limit 0.01 mg/kg food
Pb.basis_label: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
Pb.substantiation: Lead is on the Annex II point 2 not-detectable list, so the published ceiling is the 0.01 mg/kg food detection limit and not a positive migration allowance. The article consists exclusively of plastics, so this instrument governs it directly and no read-across is involved. This is a migration ceiling on the food or simulant and is never reported as a limit on the material's lead content; the material-content instruments (US CPSIA total lead in children's-product substrate, Japan Notice 370 and Korea MFDS 2024-29 percent-by-weight lead in food-contact metals and solder) are separate obligations in a different basis and are not this cell.

Cd.label: Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2: cadmium not detectable in the food or simulant, detection limit 0.002 mg/kg food
Cd.basis_label: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
Cd.substantiation: Cadmium is on the Annex II point 2 not-detectable list; the published ceiling is the 0.002 mg/kg food detection limit, the strictest element value in the instrument. The article consists exclusively of plastics, so this instrument governs it directly and no read-across is involved. The EU REACH Annex XVII cadmium restrictions on plastics, paints and recovered PVC are percent-by-weight content restrictions and are not read into this migration cell.

tAs.label: Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2: arsenic (total element) not detectable in the food or simulant, detection limit 0.01 mg/kg food
tAs.basis_label: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
tAs.substantiation: Arsenic is on the Annex II point 2 not-detectable list and the instrument states it as the total element, so this cell is total arsenic and cannot be satisfied by an inorganic-arsenic determination. The article consists exclusively of plastics, so this instrument governs it directly and no read-across is involved.

not_material.rationale: Inorganic arsenic is a dietary speciation with no separate food-contact-material instrument anywhere in the credible set: every food-contact element requirement is written on total arsenic. Arsenic migrating from a polymeric food-contact article is in any case inorganic, so the total-arsenic non-detect requirement is simultaneously the tightest achievable inorganic-arsenic ceiling and bounds this cell by identity. No separate inorganic-arsenic ceiling is published, and inorganic arsenic never substitutes for the total-arsenic cell.
not_material.bounded_by: tAs (eu_10_2011_tas_sml_nd, total arsenic not detectable at 0.01 mg/kg food)
not_material.reference_method: Total-arsenic migration determination per the tAs cell; reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation by HPLC-ICP-MS on the migration extract only where total arsenic is detected at or above the detection limit.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2 sets the element requirement as a specific migration requirement on the food or food simulant, not as a limit on the material's element content. No credible sovereign sets a species-specific migration limit for this cell.

tHg.substantiation: Mercury is on the Annex II point 2 not-detectable list, stated as the total element. The article consists exclusively of plastics, so this instrument governs it directly and no read-across is involved.

The total-mercury non-detect requirement bounds any organomercury fraction that could be present. No separate methylmercury ceiling is published, and methylmercury never substitutes for the total-mercury cell.

not_material.reference_method: Total-mercury migration determination per the tHg cell; reflex methylmercury speciation by GC-ICP-MS on the migration extract only where total mercury is detected at or above the detection limit.

Ni.label: Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 1: nickel specific migration limit 0.02 mg/kg food
Ni.basis_label: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
Ni.substantiation: Nickel carries a positive specific migration limit of 0.02 mg/kg food, the tightest positive SML in the Annex II element list. The article consists exclusively of plastics, so this instrument governs it directly and no read-across is involved. This value governs the polymeric food-contact surface only; where a food-contact component of the article is a nickel-bearing alloy, that component sits in the alloy-release control regime described in this row's component plan, because the plastics SML was not written for and is not achievable by a bare stainless-steel surface.

control.rationale: Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II lists no tin entry, and no credible sovereign sets a tin migration or release ceiling for a food-contact article of any material family. Tin is nonetheless a mandatory panel cell, because tin stabilisers in PVC compounds and tin-bearing solder are live pathways in parts of this category, so it is tested on every certified lot with no invented ceiling. This cell carries NO companion: the only sovereign tin numbers in existence are maximum levels on canned food, which are a FOOD basis on the contents of a tinplate container, and they are neither applicable to this row nor publishable as a migration ceiling. They are named as a companion only on the rows where a tinplate or crown component actually exists.
control.reference_method: EN 1186 / EN 13130 food-simulant migration testing on the finished article under its worst foreseeable use conditions (simulant, temperature and contact time selected per Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex III and Annex V; for repeat-use articles the third successive migration result governs), with ICP-MS determination of the element in the simulant.

Al.label: Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 1: aluminium specific migration limit 1 mg/kg food
Al.basis_label: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
Al.substantiation: Aluminium carries a positive specific migration limit of 1 mg/kg food, added by Reg (EU) 2016/1416. The article consists exclusively of plastics, so this instrument governs it directly and no read-across is involved. This value governs the polymeric food-contact surface; it is not applied to an aluminium metal article, because an instrument written for plastics did not contemplate an article whose food-contact surface is the element itself.

Cr.label: Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2: total chromium not detectable in the food or simulant, detection limit 0.01 mg/kg food; the 3.6 mg/kg food relaxation available on documented exclusion of chromium(VI) is declined
Cr.basis_label: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
Cr.substantiation: This total-chromium cell is deliberately published as a firm ceiling rather than the usual non-protective total-chromium screen, and the reason is structural to the instrument. Aluminium on this row is a control with the plastics SML disclosed as the companion binding the polymeric-film configuration.
food-packaging-foils-wraps.material: Two configurations in one taxonomy row: polymeric cling and barrier wrap (LDPE, PVC, PVDC, polyolefin cling film) and rolled aluminium foil, plain or paper-backed.
food-packaging-foils-wraps.components: Sample and report separately: (1) polymeric cling or barrier film food-contact surface, including plasticiser-bearing PVC cling; (2) aluminium foil bright side and matt side, tested against acidic and salted simulant at the contact temperature claimed on the pack; (3) paper backing of backed foil, where product can reach it; (4) any printed or coated foil surface; (5) core or dispenser cutting edge where it can shed onto product.

control.rationale: Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II lists no tin entry, and no credible sovereign sets a tin migration or release ceiling for a food-contact article of any material family. Tin is nonetheless a mandatory panel cell, because tin stabilisers in PVC compounds and tin-bearing solder are live pathways in parts of this category, so it is tested on every certified lot with no invented ceiling. This cell carries NO companion: the only sovereign tin numbers in existence are maximum levels on canned food, which are a FOOD basis on the contents of a tinplate container, and they are neither applicable to this row nor publishable as a migration ceiling. They are named as a companion only on the rows where a tinplate or crown component actually exists.
control.reference_method: EN 1186 / EN 13130 food-simulant migration testing on the finished article under its worst foreseeable use conditions (simulant, temperature and contact time selected per Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex III and Annex V; for repeat-use articles the third successive migration result governs), with ICP-MS determination of the element in the simulant.

control.rationale: Aluminium on this row is a control, and the carve-out is deliberate. The polymeric-film configuration is bound by the EU 10/2011 Annex II aluminium specific migration limit of 1 mg/kg food, which is disclosed as this cell's companion and is verified on every film lot. The ALUMINIUM-FOIL configuration is not: rolled aluminium foil is a metal article whose food-contact surface is aluminium itself, metals and alloys are a Regulation 1935/2004 Annex I material family for which the EU has adopted no specific measure, and no credible sovereign sets an aluminium release ceiling for a metal foil. Publishing the plastics SML against aluminium foil would take a number written for a polymer surface and assert it of an article made of the element, which is a misapplication rather than a conservative reading, and it is documented that aluminium foil in contact with acidic or salted food exceeds it. HMTc therefore mandates release testing of the foil configuration under the declared contact conditions with no invented ceiling, and reports the film and foil configurations separately rather than pooling them.
control.reference_method: Food-simulant release testing on each food-contact metal component under worst foreseeable use conditions (acidic simulant at the article's stated cooking or holding temperature and duration; for repeat-use articles the third successive release result governs), ICP-MS determination in the simulant, plus alloy-composition verification of every food-contact component by ICP-OES after acid digestion (XRF for screening only). Foil tested against 3 percent acetic acid and against a salted simulant at the maximum contact temperature and duration claimed on the pack, reporting bright and matt sides separately.

food-storage-plastic-containers.native_basis_label: specific element migration INTO FOOD OR A FOOD SIMULANT from the polymeric food-contact surface, µg/kg of food, determined by the Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex III to V simulant, temperature and contact-time conventions. This is a MIGRATION basis and not a total-content basis: no cell on this row limits how much of an element the material CONTAINS, and no cell on this row is expressed per kg of material.
food-storage-plastic-containers.scope_note: Repeat-use plastic articles consisting exclusively of plastics, directly within Reg (EU) 10/2011. Because these are repeat-use articles the migration convention is the third successive migration, which is the value that governs; a first-migration result overstates compliance and is not accepted. Microwave and freezer claims extend the contact conditions and must be tested at the claimed extremes.
food-storage-plastic-containers.material: Repeat-use polypropylene, Tritan copolyester, polycarbonate or HDPE bodies, frequently with a separate lid and a silicone or thermoplastic-elastomer seal.
food-storage-plastic-containers.components: Sample and report separately: (1) container body interior; (2) lid food-contact face; (3) silicone or elastomer sealing ring, which sits outside Reg (EU) 10/2011 by its Art. 2(2)(c) exclusion of silicones and takes these ceilings by disclosed read-across; (4) any vent or valve component; (5) printed measurement graduations on an interior surface; (6) recycled-content resin streams as their own lot.
food-storage-plastic-containers.audit_scope: food.contact|food contact|plastic food|utensil|cookware|cooking utensil|kitchen|tableware|crockery|ceramic|porcelain|earthenware|glaze|enamel|glassware|hollowware|packaging and containers|food-contact surface
food-storage-plastic-containers.basis_guard_note: Only an instrument expressed as specific element migration into food or a food simulant may anchor a cell on this row. The guard exists to reject the three foreign bases that surround this category and would otherwise look plausible: the FOOD basis (canned-food tin maximum levels, which limit the contents and not the article), the MATERIAL-CONTENT basis (CPSIA total lead in substrate, EU REACH Annex XVII cadmium percent-by-weight restrictions, RoHS homogeneous-material limits, Japan Notice 370 and Korea MFDS percent-by-weight lead in food-contact metals), and the ARTICLE-EXTRACTION basis of the toy regime (EU 2009/48 Annex II Part III and ASTM F963 soluble limits, which are element migration from scraped-off or coated TOY material into 0.07 M hydrochloric acid, expressed per kg of MATERIAL, not per kg of food). Any of those would fail this guard and resolve to a gap rather than publish in the wrong basis.

Pb.label: Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2: lead not detectable in the food or simulant, detection limit 0.01 mg/kg food
Pb.basis_label: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
Pb.substantiation: Lead is on the Annex II point 2 not-detectable list, so the published ceiling is the 0.01 mg/kg food detection limit and not a positive migration allowance. The body and lid consist exclusively of plastics and are within this instrument's direct scope; the silicone sealing ring is excluded from the instrument by Art. 2(2)(c) and takes the same value by disclosed read-across, which changes no number. This is a migration ceiling on the food or simulant and is never reported as a limit on the material's lead content; the material-content instruments (US CPSIA total lead in children's-product substrate, Japan Notice 370 and Korea MFDS 2024-29 percent-by-weight lead in food-contact metals and solder) are separate obligations in a different basis and are not this cell.

Cd.label: Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2: cadmium not detectable in the food or simulant, detection limit 0.002 mg/kg food
Cd.basis_label: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
Cd.substantiation: Cadmium is on the Annex II point 2 not-detectable list; the published ceiling is the 0.002 mg/kg food detection limit, the strictest element value in the instrument. The body and lid consist exclusively of plastics and are within this instrument's direct scope; the silicone sealing ring is excluded from the instrument by Art. 2(2)(c) and takes the same value by disclosed read-across, which changes no number. The EU REACH Annex XVII cadmium restrictions on plastics, paints and recovered PVC are percent-by-weight content restrictions and are not read into this migration cell.

tAs.label: Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2: arsenic (total element) not detectable in the food or simulant, detection limit 0.01 mg/kg food
tAs.basis_label: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
tAs.substantiation: Arsenic is on the Annex II point 2 not-detectable list and the instrument states it as the total element, so this cell is total arsenic and cannot be satisfied by an inorganic-arsenic determination. The body and lid consist exclusively of plastics and are within this instrument's direct scope; the silicone sealing ring is excluded from the instrument by Art. 2(2)(c) and takes the same value by disclosed read-across, which changes no number.

not_material.rationale: Inorganic arsenic is a dietary speciation with no separate food-contact-material instrument anywhere in the credible set: every food-contact element requirement is written on total arsenic. Arsenic migrating from a polymeric food-contact article is in any case inorganic, so the total-arsenic non-detect requirement is simultaneously the tightest achievable inorganic-arsenic ceiling and bounds this cell by identity. No separate inorganic-arsenic ceiling is published, and inorganic arsenic never substitutes for the total-arsenic cell.
not_material.bounded_by: tAs (eu_10_2011_tas_sml_nd, total arsenic not detectable at 0.01 mg/kg food)
not_material.reference_method: Total-arsenic migration determination per the tAs cell; reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation by HPLC-ICP-MS on the migration extract only where total arsenic is detected at or above the detection limit.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2 sets the element requirement as a specific migration requirement on the food or food simulant, not as a limit on the material's element content. No credible sovereign sets a species-specific migration limit for this cell.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU (Reg (EU) 1935/2004 framework + Annex I material families; Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II element list, as amended by 2016/1416 and 2020/1245); UK (retained Reg 10/2011); US (FDA food-contact substances, 21 CFR 174-190: no element migration ceiling for these elements); Codex (no food-contact-material standard); AU-NZ (FSANZ Food Standards Code 1.4.3 and 3.2.2: no element migration ceiling); Canada (Food and Drugs Act s.4 / letter-of-no-objection route, no numeric element migration ceiling); Hong Kong (Cap 132 subsidiary legislation: food limits only).

tHg.label: Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2: mercury (total element) not detectable in the food or simulant, detection limit 0.01 mg/kg food
tHg.basis_label: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
tHg.substantiation: Mercury is on the Annex II point 2 not-detectable list, stated as the total element. The body and lid consist exclusively of plastics and are within this instrument's direct scope; the silicone sealing ring is excluded from the instrument by Art. 2(2)(c) and takes the same value by disclosed read-across, which changes no number.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is formed by microbial methylation in aquatic food chains. A cured polymer, a fired glaze, a metal alloy and a coated article contain no methylation pathway, and no credible sovereign sets a methylmercury requirement for any food-contact material. The total-mercury non-detect requirement bounds any organomercury fraction that could be present. No separate methylmercury ceiling is published, and methylmercury never substitutes for the total-mercury cell.
not_material.bounded_by: tHg (eu_10_2011_thg_sml_nd, total mercury not detectable at 0.01 mg/kg food)
not_material.reference_method: Total-mercury migration determination per the tHg cell; reflex methylmercury speciation by GC-ICP-MS on the migration extract only where total mercury is detected at or above the detection limit.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2 sets the element requirement as a specific migration requirement on the food or food simulant, not as a limit on the material's element content. No credible sovereign sets a species-specific migration limit for this cell.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU (Reg (EU) 1935/2004 framework + Annex I material families; Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II element list, as amended by 2016/1416 and 2020/1245); UK (retained Reg 10/2011); US (FDA food-contact substances, 21 CFR 174-190: no element migration ceiling for these elements); Codex (no food-contact-material standard); AU-NZ (FSANZ Food Standards Code 1.4.3 and 3.2.2: no element migration ceiling); Canada (Food and Drugs Act s.4 / letter-of-no-objection route, no numeric element migration ceiling); Hong Kong (Cap 132 subsidiary legislation: food limits only).

Ni.label: Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 1: nickel specific migration limit 0.02 mg/kg food
Ni.basis_label: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
Ni.substantiation: Nickel carries a positive specific migration limit of 0.02 mg/kg food, the tightest positive SML in the Annex II element list. The body and lid consist exclusively of plastics and are within this instrument's direct scope; the silicone sealing ring is excluded from the instrument by Art. 2(2)(c) and takes the same value by disclosed read-across, which changes no number. This value governs the polymeric food-contact surface only; where a food-contact component of the article is a nickel-bearing alloy, that component sits in the alloy-release control regime described in this row's component plan, because the plastics SML was not written for and is not achievable by a bare stainless-steel surface.

control.rationale: Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II lists no tin entry, and no credible sovereign sets a tin migration or release ceiling for a food-contact article of any material family. Tin is nonetheless a mandatory panel cell, because tin stabilisers in PVC compounds and tin-bearing solder are live pathways in parts of this category, so it is tested on every certified lot with no invented ceiling. This cell carries NO companion: the only sovereign tin numbers in existence are maximum levels on canned food, which are a FOOD basis on the contents of a tinplate container, and they are neither applicable to this row nor publishable as a migration ceiling. They are named as a companion only on the rows where a tinplate or crown component actually exists.
control.reference_method: EN 1186 / EN 13130 food-simulant migration testing on the finished article under its worst foreseeable use conditions (simulant, temperature and contact time selected per Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex III and Annex V; for repeat-use articles the third successive migration result governs), with ICP-MS determination of the element in the simulant.

Al.label: Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 1: aluminium specific migration limit 1 mg/kg food
Al.basis_label: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
Al.substantiation: Aluminium carries a positive specific migration limit of 1 mg/kg food, added by Reg (EU) 2016/1416. The body and lid consist exclusively of plastics and are within this instrument's direct scope; the silicone sealing ring is excluded from the instrument by Art. 2(2)(c) and takes the same value by disclosed read-across, which changes no number. This value governs the polymeric food-contact surface; it is not applied to an aluminium metal article, because an instrument written for plastics did not contemplate an article whose food-contact surface is the element itself.

Cr.label: Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2: total chromium not detectable in the food or simulant, detection limit 0.01 mg/kg food; the 3.6 mg/kg food relaxation available on documented exclusion of chromium(VI) is declined
Cr.basis_label: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
Cr.substantiation: This total-chromium cell is deliberately published as a firm ceiling rather than the usual non-protective total-chromium screen, and the reason is structural to the instrument. Annex II point 2 as amended by Reg (EU) 2020/1245 sets total chromium at not detectable and permits a relaxed 3.6 mg/kg food limit only where the operator documents that chromium(VI) is absent. The non-detect branch therefore exists precisely because hexavalent chromium cannot be assumed absent, which makes it the hexavalent-chromium-conservative form of the requirement rather than a chromium(III)-dominated artefact. HMTc publishes the non-detect branch and declines the relaxation, and the hexavalent-chromium cell is bounded by this value. The body and lid consist exclusively of plastics and are within this instrument's direct scope; the silicone sealing ring is excluded from the instrument by Art. 2(2)(c) and takes the same value by disclosed read-across, which changes no number.

not_material.rationale: Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2 controls hexavalent chromium through the total-chromium requirement rather than through a separate species limit: total chromium must be not detectable, and the relaxed 3.6 mg/kg food value becomes available only where the operator documents that chromium(VI) is absent. HMTc declines that relaxation, so every certified article is held to total chromium not detectable at 0.01 mg/kg food, which bounds hexavalent chromium at or below the same value. No credible sovereign sets a hexavalent-chromium migration limit for a food-contact material, so no separate species ceiling is published; hexavalent chromium never substitutes for the total-chromium cell.
not_material.bounded_by: Cr (eu_10_2011_crtotal_sml_nd, total chromium not detectable at 0.01 mg/kg food, relaxation declined)
not_material.reference_method: Total-chromium migration determination per the Cr cell; reflex hexavalent-chromium speciation by ion-chromatography ICP-MS on the migration extract where total chromium is detected at or above the detection limit, and on any chromate-conversion-coated or passivated food-contact component regardless of the total result.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2 sets the element requirement as a specific migration requirement on the food or food simulant, not as a limit on the material's element content. No credible sovereign sets a species-specific migration limit for this cell.

food-storage-plastic-containers.cross_reference: Category 9 (Infant and Child Contact Products) governs any article in this row that is marketed for ages 0-5; the taxonomy boundary rule routes infant bottles, nipples and toddler drinkware there even though they are food-contact items.

food-storage-glass-containers.name: Glass food storage containers
food-storage-glass-containers.native_basis: element release from the glaze, enamel or glass into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
food-storage-glass-containers.native_basis_label: element RELEASE FROM THE GLAZE, VITREOUS ENAMEL OR GLASS NETWORK INTO FOOD OR A FOOD SIMULANT, µg/kg of food, determined by the 4 percent (v/v) acetic acid filled-article or contact-surface extraction convention used for this material family, with decoration within 20 mm of the lip determined separately. This is the glaze-and-glass RELEASE basis; it is deliberately NOT the Reg (EU) 10/2011 plastics-simulant convention, and a plastics specific migration limit is never substituted for a release limit on this family.
food-storage-glass-containers.scope_note: The principal food-contact material is the glass network, whose release regime is absent from the register, so the row is a control. Lids and gaskets are separate components under their own regimes. Oven-to-table and freezer-to-oven claims extend the contact conditions and must be tested at the claimed extremes, because release from a glass surface is temperature-dependent.
food-storage-glass-containers.material: Soda-lime or borosilicate glass bodies, frequently with a plastic lid and a silicone gasket, and often with printed exterior graduations or decoration.
food-storage-glass-containers.components: Sample and report separately: (1) interior glass surface, filled-article extraction at the highest claimed use temperature; (2) plastic lid food-contact face, bound by the plastics migration ceilings; (3) silicone gasket, bound by the plastics ceilings by disclosed read-across; (4) printed exterior graduation or decoration, tested where it lies within 20 mm of the lip; (5) any interior decoration or fill-line print, tested as a decoration.

food-storage-glass-containers.basis_guard: element release from the glaze, enamel or glass into food
food-storage-glass-containers.basis_guard_note: Only an instrument expressed as specific element migration into food or a food simulant may anchor a cell on this row. The guard exists to reject the three foreign bases that surround this category and would otherwise look plausible: the FOOD basis (canned-food tin maximum levels, which limit the contents and not the article), the MATERIAL-CONTENT basis (CPSIA total lead in substrate, EU REACH Annex XVII cadmium percent-by-weight restrictions, RoHS homogeneous-material limits, Japan Notice 370 and Korea MFDS percent-by-weight lead in food-contact metals), and the ARTICLE-EXTRACTION basis of the toy regime (EU 2009/48 Annex II Part III and ASTM F963 soluble limits, which are element migration from scraped-off or coated TOY material into 0.07 M hydrochloric acid, expressed per kg of MATERIAL, not per kg of food). Any of those would fail this guard and resolve to a gap rather than publish in the wrong basis. On this control row the guard is declaratory as well as operative: it records the only basis in which a future ingested instrument would be allowed to supply this row's numbers, so that a content limit, a food limit, a water limit or a plastics specific migration limit cannot later be dropped in as this row's release ceiling. The plastics clause is deliberately absent from this guard: a Reg (EU) 10/2011 value named here would fail the guard and resolve to a gap.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign release ceiling for this material family is present in the HMTc regulatory register. Glazed ceramic, vitreous enamel, glass and applied decoration are governed in the real world by a dedicated lead-and-cadmium release regime (EU Council Directive 84/500/EEC as amended by 2005/31/EC for ceramic articles, and the US FDA compliance-policy guides on lead in ceramicware and decorated glassware), and by California Proposition 65 consent judgments on tableware. None of those instruments has been ingested into data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, and this build refuses to substitute the plastics specific migration limits for a glaze-release limit: the two are different extractions on different material families and the substitution would be a basis conflation. The cell is a control until the release regime is ingested through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway, and the gap is recorded. Lead is the dominant pathway for this material family: lead-fluxed and lead-bisilicate glazes, lead-bearing on-glaze enamels and applied decoration, and under-fired or acid-attacked glaze surfaces all release lead into acidic food. It is the single cell where the absent release regime matters most, and the gap is recorded rather than papered over with a plastics value. On a glass storage container the release surface is the glass network and any interior or near-lip decoration; the lid and gasket are separate polymer components with their own published ceilings, reported separately and never averaged into this row's result.
control.reference_method: Release testing on the filled or contact-surface article using 4 percent (v/v) acetic acid at the article's stated use temperature and duration (the release convention used for glazed, enamelled and glass food-contact articles), ICP-MS determination in the extract, with a separate determination on any decoration lying within 20 mm of the lip or on any interior decoration.

tHg.label: Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2: mercury (total element) not detectable in the food or simulant, detection limit 0.01 mg/kg food
tHg.basis_label: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
tHg.substantiation: Mercury is on the Annex II point 2 not-detectable list, stated as the total element. Plastic lids and plastic gaskets in caps and closures are within this instrument's direct scope under Art. 2(1)(a) and Art. 2(1)(d); silicone gaskets take the same values by disclosed read-across.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is formed by microbial methylation in aquatic food chains. A cured polymer, a fired glaze, a metal alloy and a coated article contain no methylation pathway, and no credible sovereign sets a methylmercury requirement for any food-contact material. The total-mercury non-detect requirement bounds any organomercury fraction that could be present. No separate methylmercury ceiling is published, and methylmercury never substitutes for the total-mercury cell.
not_material.bounded_by: tHg (eu_10_2011_thg_sml_nd, total mercury not detectable at 0.01 mg/kg food)
not_material.reference_method: Total-mercury migration determination per the tHg cell; reflex methylmercury speciation by GC-ICP-MS on the migration extract only where total mercury is detected at or above the detection limit.

Ni.label: Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 1: nickel specific migration limit 0.02 mg/kg food
Ni.basis_label: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
Ni.substantiation: Nickel carries a positive specific migration limit of 0.02 mg/kg food, the tightest positive SML in the Annex II element list. Plastic lids and plastic gaskets in caps and closures are within this instrument's direct scope under Art. 2(1)(a) and Art. 2(1)(d); silicone gaskets take the same values by disclosed read-across. This value governs the polymeric food-contact surface only; where a food-contact component of the article is a nickel-bearing alloy, that component sits in the alloy-release control regime described in this row's component plan, because the plastics SML was not written for and is not achievable by a bare stainless-steel surface.

control.rationale: Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II lists no tin entry, and no credible sovereign sets a tin migration or release ceiling for a food-contact article of any material family. Tin is nonetheless a mandatory panel cell, because tin stabilisers in PVC compounds and tin-bearing solder are live pathways in parts of this category, so it is tested on every certified lot with no invented ceiling. This cell carries NO companion: the only sovereign tin numbers in existence are maximum levels on canned food, which are a FOOD basis on the contents of a tinplate container, and they are neither applicable to this row nor publishable as a migration ceiling. They are named as a companion only on the rows where a tinplate or crown component actually exists.
control.reference_method: EN 1186 / EN 13130 food-simulant migration testing on the finished article under its worst foreseeable use conditions (simulant, temperature and contact time selected per Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex III and Annex V; for repeat-use articles the third successive migration result governs), with ICP-MS determination of the element in the simulant.

Al.label: Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 1: aluminium specific migration limit 1 mg/kg food
Al.basis_label: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
Al.substantiation: Aluminium carries a positive specific migration limit of 1 mg/kg food, added by Reg (EU) 2016/1416. Plastic lids and plastic gaskets in caps and closures are within this instrument's direct scope under Art. 2(1)(a) and Art. 2(1)(d); silicone gaskets take the same values by disclosed read-across. This value governs the polymeric food-contact surface; it is not applied to an aluminium metal article, because an instrument written for plastics did not contemplate an article whose food-contact surface is the element itself.

Cr.label: Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2: total chromium not detectable in the food or simulant, detection limit 0.01 mg/kg food; the 3.6 mg/kg food relaxation available on documented exclusion of chromium(VI) is declined
Cr.basis_label: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
Cr.substantiation: This total-chromium cell is deliberately published as a firm ceiling rather than the usual non-protective total-chromium screen, and the reason is structural to the instrument. Annex II point 2 as amended by Reg (EU) 2020/1245 sets total chromium at not detectable and permits a relaxed 3.6 mg/kg food limit only where the operator documents that chromium(VI) is absent. The non-detect branch therefore exists precisely because hexavalent chromium cannot be assumed absent, which makes it the hexavalent-chromium-conservative form of the requirement rather than a chromium(III)-dominated artefact. HMTc publishes the non-detect branch and declines the relaxation, and the hexavalent-chromium cell is bounded by this value. Plastic lids and plastic gaskets in caps and closures are within this instrument's direct scope under Art. 2(1)(a) and Art. 2(1)(d); silicone gaskets take the same values by disclosed read-across.

not_material.rationale: Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2 controls hexavalent chromium through the total-chromium requirement rather than through a separate species limit: total chromium must be not detectable, and the relaxed 3.6 mg/kg food value becomes available only where the operator documents that chromium(VI) is absent. HMTc declines that relaxation, so every certified article is held to total chromium not detectable at 0.01 mg/kg food, which bounds hexavalent chromium at or below the same value. No credible sovereign sets a hexavalent-chromium migration limit for a food-contact material, so no separate species ceiling is published; hexavalent chromium never substitutes for the total-chromium cell.
not_material.bounded_by: Cr (eu_10_2011_crtotal_sml_nd, total chromium not detectable at 0.01 mg/kg food, relaxation declined)
not_material.reference_method: Total-chromium migration determination per the Cr cell; reflex hexavalent-chromium speciation by ion-chromatography ICP-MS on the migration extract where total chromium is detected at or above the detection limit, and on any chromate-conversion-coated or passivated food-contact component regardless of the total result.

tableware-ceramicware.name: Ceramicware
tableware-ceramicware.native_basis: element release from the glaze, enamel or glass into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
tableware-ceramicware.native_basis_label: element RELEASE FROM THE GLAZE, VITREOUS ENAMEL OR GLASS NETWORK INTO FOOD OR A FOOD SIMULANT, µg/kg of food, determined by the 4 percent (v/v) acetic acid filled-article or contact-surface extraction convention used for this material family, with decoration within 20 mm of the lip determined separately. This is the glaze-and-glass RELEASE basis; it is deliberately NOT the Reg (EU) 10/2011 plastics-simulant convention, and a plastics specific migration limit is never substituted for a release limit on this family.
tableware-ceramicware.scope_note: Glazed ceramic food-contact articles: plates, bowls, mugs, serving and cooking ware. This is the highest-risk row in the category and the one where the register gap bites hardest, because the dedicated lead-and-cadmium release regime for ceramic articles (EU Council Directive 84/500/EEC as amended by 2005/31/EC, and the US FDA compliance-policy guide on lead in ceramicware, together with the California Proposition 65 tableware consent judgments) is not present in data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv. The row is a control, the gap is recorded, and the plastics migration limits are NOT substituted: a 4 percent acetic acid glaze-release extraction and a food-simulant plastics migration test are different extractions on different material families, and equating them would be a basis conflation.
tableware-ceramicware.material: Earthenware, stoneware, porcelain and bone china bodies with fired glaze; on-glaze and in-glaze enamel decoration; imported and artisanal ware with lead-fluxed or lead-bisilicate glaze; unglazed or under-fired interior surfaces.
tableware-ceramicware.components: Sample and report separately: (1) interior glazed food-contact surface, filled-article extraction; (2) lip and rim band, including any decoration within 20 mm of the lip; (3) on-glaze or in-glaze enamel decoration on any interior surface; (4) unglazed foot ring, crazed or crawled glaze areas, and any repair or touch-up; (5) handle and spout joins where glaze pools or thins; (6) each glaze and enamel colour as its own lot, because glaze release is colour-specific and a single-colour result does not represent a decorated range.

tableware-ceramicware.basis_guard: element release from the glaze, enamel or glass into food
tableware-ceramicware.basis_guard_note: Only an instrument expressed as specific element migration into food or a food simulant may anchor a cell on this row. The guard exists to reject the three foreign bases that surround this category and would otherwise look plausible: the FOOD basis (canned-food tin maximum levels, which limit the contents and not the article), the MATERIAL-CONTENT basis (CPSIA total lead in substrate, EU REACH Annex XVII cadmium percent-by-weight restrictions, RoHS homogeneous-material limits, Japan Notice 370 and Korea MFDS percent-by-weight lead in food-contact metals), and the ARTICLE-EXTRACTION basis of the toy regime (EU 2009/48 Annex II Part III and ASTM F963 soluble limits, which are element migration from scraped-off or coated TOY material into 0.07 M hydrochloric acid, expressed per kg of MATERIAL, not per kg of food). Any of those would fail this guard and resolve to a gap rather than publish in the wrong basis. On this control row the guard is declaratory as well as operative: it records the only basis in which a future ingested instrument would be allowed to supply this row's numbers, so that a content limit, a food limit, a water limit or a plastics specific migration limit cannot later be dropped in as this row's release ceiling. The plastics clause is deliberately absent from this guard: a Reg (EU) 10/2011 value named here would fail the guard and resolve to a gap.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign release ceiling for this material family is present in the HMTc regulatory register. Glazed ceramic, vitreous enamel, glass and applied decoration are governed in the real world by a dedicated lead-and-cadmium release regime (EU Council Directive 84/500/EEC as amended by 2005/31/EC for ceramic articles, and the US FDA compliance-policy guides on lead in ceramicware and decorated glassware), and by California Proposition 65 consent judgments on tableware. None of those instruments has been ingested into data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, and this build refuses to substitute the plastics specific migration limits for a glaze-release limit: the two are different extractions on different material families and the substitution would be a basis conflation. The cell is a control until the release regime is ingested through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway, and the gap is recorded. Lead is the dominant pathway for this material family: lead-fluxed and lead-bisilicate glazes, lead-bearing on-glaze enamels and applied decoration, and under-fired or acid-attacked glaze surfaces all release lead into acidic food. It is the single cell where the absent release regime matters most, and the gap is recorded rather than papered over with a plastics value. Ceramicware is the row for which the absent release regime is most consequential, so the control is written to be operative: every glaze and enamel colour is tested as its own lot, the lip band is tested separately, and a detection triggers escalation rather than a comparison against a borrowed number.
control.reference_method: Release testing on the filled or contact-surface article using 4 percent (v/v) acetic acid at the article's stated use temperature and duration (the release convention used for glazed, enamelled and glass food-contact articles), ICP-MS determination in the extract, with a separate determination on any decoration lying within 20 mm of the lip or on any interior decoration.

tableware-glassware.name: Glassware
